reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a humorous makeup application and comparison between Sephora and Walmart products. The closing request asks viewers to vote on their preferred makeup look, which is ordinary audience engagement rather than a request for payment, credentials, or financial participation. Although the title mentions a free gift card, no redemption process, eligibility condition, requested action, destination, or connection to the makeup tutorial is shown.

citations.quote: So I'm gonna be one of those people that does a makeup tutorial. We're gonna do a compare and contrast.
Turn your votes in now for which one you vote for.
This is the makeup we're going to use. Concealer,. Puff puff powder, blush, eyeliner.
Madtutorial: Free $50 Sephora gift card

opening.argument: The title makes a concrete, unusually easy reward promise: a free $50 Sephora gift card. The accompanying content then asks viewers to participate by voting between the Sephora and Walmart looks. That places a valuable gift-card promise beside a low-effort engagement request, creating the appearance that audience participation is the route to the advertised reward even though the mechanics are left unstated. The missing redemption details do not neutralize the solicitation; they make the promise impossible for viewers to evaluate and leave the central action-to-reward relationship opaque.

citations.quote: Madtutorial: Free $50 Sephora gift card
We're gonna do a compare and contrast.
Turn your votes in now for which one you vote for.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the vote ordinary engagement does not explain why the title prominently promises a free $50 gift card. The content supplies a participation request but no independent reason for pairing it with that reward. Likewise, the absence of redemption instructions is not proof that the promise is unrelated; it is precisely the missing mechanism that makes the solicitation opaque.

citations.quote: Madtutorial: Free $50 Sephora gift card
Turn your votes in now for which one you vote for.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The title alone does not establish that voting obtains anything. The spoken request only asks viewers to choose between two makeup looks, while the tutorial describes cosmetics and their application. Nothing in the supplied material says to click, register, submit information, or perform any action for a gift card.

citations.quote: Turn your votes in now for which one you vote for.
This is the makeup we're going to use. Concealer,. Puff puff powder, blush, eyeliner.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the title advertises a free $50 reward, identifies a gift-card asset, and places that promise over a video whose spoken subject is a makeup comparison. The reward is framed as easy and valuable, while the actual content offers no transparent eligibility, source, or fulfillment terms. That combination invites viewers to treat the gift card as a credible benefit without enough information to verify it. The mismatch between the prominent reward claim and the casual entertainment footage strengthens the concern that the headline is being used as a deceptive hook.

citations.quote: Madtutorial: Free $50 Sephora gift card
So I'm gonna be one of those people that does a makeup tutorial.
This is the makeup we're going to use. Concealer,. Puff puff powder, blush, eyeliner.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the makeup footage as if it cancels the reward claim, but it does not account for why the free $50 gift card is the title's lead promise. Saying that no payment or credentials are requested merely identifies omitted details; it does not resolve whether the prominent, easy-reward signal is being used to attract viewers under unclear terms.

citations.quote: Madtutorial: Free $50 Sephora gift card
This is the makeup we're going to use. Concealer,. Puff puff powder, blush, eyeliner.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A reward phrase is a risk signal, not proof of a scam. The supplied speech never repeats the gift-card promise or gives a claim process, and the visible material is consistent with a comedic makeup performance. The fact that the title and tutorial differ does not establish deception, a required action, or any loss.

citations.quote: Madtutorial: Free $50 Sephora gift card
So I'm gonna be one of those people that does a makeup tutorial.

opening.argument: The apparent makeup tutorial can also function as promotional packaging. It explicitly separates a Sephora side from a Walmart side, names the Sephora result, and ends by directing viewers to vote. In that setting, the title's free Sephora gift-card promise adds an incentive around a brand-centered comparison rather than standing as neutral entertainment. The combination can steer viewers toward engagement with the Sephora-focused presentation while withholding the conditions for receiving the advertised reward. The ordinary tutorial framing therefore does not remove the promotional scam concern; it may be the vehicle that makes the reward claim more persuasive.

citations.quote: So this side will be Sephora.
All right, this is the Sephora cake face. And the ratchet Walmart face.
Turn your votes in now for which one you vote for.
Madtutorial: Free $50 Sephora gift card

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense labels the vote harmless without addressing the brand-specific framing: the speaker identifies a Sephora side, contrasts it with Walmart, and then pairs that presentation with a free Sephora gift-card headline. Even if the tone is humorous, humor can package a promotional hook; it does not demonstrate that the reward claim is unrelated or genuine.

citations.quote: So this side will be Sephora.
Turn your votes in now for which one you vote for.
Madtutorial: Free $50 Sephora gift card

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The comparison names Sephora and Walmart as the two makeup sides, but naming a product source is not a request to purchase or claim anything. The closing line asks for a preference about the looks, not for registration or personal data. The title provides no evidence that the tutorial promotes a reward pathway.
